results.reason: The memo never mentions the Delivery Date conflict between Schedule §1.1 (date of shipment) and MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It also never discusses the effect on late-delivery remedies, risk or payment for transit delays.
Because the Delivery Date conflict is not identified, the memo gives no fix. It neither conforms the Schedule to the MSA nor states which document controls on conflict.

Issue 2 identifies MSA §4.3 as covering 'all housings and similar components worldwide' against the Term Sheet's Series 7 / U.S. scope. It explains that this blocks other suppliers and non-U.S. plants, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings for U.S. purchases.

Issue 3 identifies §15.2 as letting Verdane assign freely, including to a competitor, while Harlow needs consent. It cites the risk to supply and to confidential Specifications. It recommends requiring Harlow's prior consent or, at minimum, barring competitors and adding a change-of-control termination right.

Issue 1 explains that Amendment §2.1/§2.2 removes gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the exclusions, so those losses become capped at 12 months of fees. It recommends rejecting the change and restoring the original exclusions.
The memo states the §11.1 cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months. It also states the original §11.2 exclusions are gross negligence, willful misconduct and the §10.1 IP Indemnity.
The memo states Term Sheet §3.1 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings within the United States. It uses that as the baseline for comparing MSA §4.3.
The memo states New York governs under MSA §16.1. It cites no cases or statutes, and flags its general New York public-policy point and the enforceability points as needing confirmation.

The memo is addressed to the partner with a bottom line. Each issue gives the document and section, why it matters to Harlow, and a recommended fix. Issues are ranked by importance, and there is a section on assumptions and open points.
The memo uses the Term Sheet only as evidence of the agreed deal. It expressly says the 3-year term and the 45-day payment terms match and are not defects.

The memo attributes exclusivity to MSA §4.3 and assignment to MSA §15.2 correctly, and the party positions are correct. The legal point is general and flagged for confirmation, with no invented citations.
